newsitem.title: UK: Metals Outlook - Copper's mood sours on stocks.
newsitem.headline: Metals Outlook - Copper's mood sours on stocks.

text.p: Copper's recent buoyancy has taken a sharp knock amid stock increases and easier spreads.
Prices could head lower this week, analysts said.
After three consecutive London Metal Exchange (LME) stock builds, values last week tumbled some $100 per tonne in volatile trading to finish Friday's kerb at $2,138.

But they edged up in late trade to around $2,160 suggesting that a volatile market might bring surprises. Increasingly tight cash/threes backwardation, which hit a high of $285 in late November, also eased as lending started to flow in and started the week at around $145-160.
A test of support at $2,100, and then possibly $2,000, looked increasingly likely in the near term, analysts said.

"The odds are stacked against copper. A couple of weeks ago backwardation was approaching $300 and stocks were very, very low. It's amazing how sentiment has changed overnight," said analyst Robin Bhar of brokers Brandeis.
"It's not to say there's going to collapse in prices, but a lot of bullish factors which were propelling the market upward have now subsided," he said.
Stocks would continue to play a key role in setting the tone for the market in the absence of other fundamental news.
Uncertainty remained, dealers said, as the market anxiously pondered whether three rises signalled a trend.
But the likelihood of increases in stocks was expected to intensify towards the year-end as spare metal was likely to be attracted to the LME over the slow holiday period.
Consumer trade buying might emerge to support copper as prices declined. "But the last thing consumers want to do is purchase metal this side of Christmas," Bhar said.
Anticipation of a run-up in prices ahead of last Wednesday's options expiry fizzled out after the declaration ended smoothly without December copper approaching the $2,600 strike price.
That might leave the market more comfortable to go short, analysts said.
"People didn't want to buy the market nor sell the market because of the declaration, but now that it's out of the way... the risk of selling isn't as great as a week ago," Bhar said.
Aluminium was likely to continue following flagship copper closely, particularly as consumer buying had dried up since prices started consolidating.
"It's done enough for now, and needs to consolidate. The gap at $1,460-$1,470 needs to be filled before it can go higher," Bhar said.
